Exemption allowed subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

1. This petition has been filed seeking quashing of FIR No.330/2018 under sections 498A/406/34 IPC PS Jagatpuri on the ground that the parties have arrived at a settlement vide settlement /MOU dated 29th August, 2022 arrived at with the facilitation of Mediation Centre, Karkardooma Courts,
which is on record of this Court.
2. Petitioner nos. 1 to 4 and respondent no.2-complainant are present in the Court have been duly identified by the Investigating Officer and their respective counsels.
3. Marriage of petitioner No. 1 and respondent No. 2 has since been dissolved vide decree of divorce by mutual consent dated 3rd March, 2022; no child was born out of wedlock.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 14:57:06 4.

As per the settlement, a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- is to be paid to respondent no. 2 by the petitioner no.1 at this stage which is tendered by way of Demand Draft No. DD No. 940367 dated 17th May,
2023 drawn on Canara bank which she has received and acknowledged in the Court.
She further submits that she has no objection to quashing of the FIR.

sentences.text: petitioners being remote and bleak, there is no use continuing with proceedings of the present FIR as it would be a misuse of the process of the Court and an unnecessary burden on the State exchequer.
Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
Consequently, the FIR No.330/2018 under sections 498A/406/34 IPC PS Jagatpuri and proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
6. Parties shall abide by the terms of settlement.
7. Petition stands disposed of accordingly.
8. Pending applications (if any) are disposed of as infructuous.
9. Order be uploaded on the website of this Court.
ANISH DAYAL, J MAY 18, 2023/sm
